meta.title: GigLedger — Know what you actually take home
meta.description: A simple ledger for freelancers. Track income, platform fees, expenses, and fixed costs, then see your true profit and tax reserve target.
meta.ogTitle: Know what you actually take home.
meta.ogDescription: One ledger for freelance income, fixed costs, true profit, and tax reserves.

hero.sub: Track income, platform fees, expenses, and fixed costs in one ledger. See your true profit, and how much to set aside for taxes.
hero.visualAria: GigLedger dashboard preview with sample income, fees, fixed costs, profit, and tax reserve.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.heading: Your saved ledger.
dashboard.subheading: These entries are loaded from your GigLedger account. Add more below, then save changes with Google.

daily.title: Your daily floor.
daily.body: Rent. Software. Insurance. The costs that keep running whether you bill a client or not. GigLedger turns them into one number you can act on.
daily.note: Example: $900 in monthly business fixed costs at 100% business use.

features.title: Everything you need to see what's left.

cards.title: Scattered income, one place.
cards.body: Add or import earnings from Upwork, Fiverr, Stripe, and direct clients. Keep platform fees and net payouts attached to every entry.

cards.title: Fixed costs, finally visible.
cards.body: Turn recurring business costs into a daily number, with business-use percentages and no double counting.

cards.title: Set aside the right amount.
cards.body: Set your own reserve rate, with a 25%-30% US self-employment reference range. Clearly labeled as an estimate, not tax advice.

cards.title: Reports you can hand over.
cards.body: Monthly, quarterly, and annual views you can export for your accountant, lender, or landlord.

steps.title: Three steps to a clearer number.

items.title: Add your fixed costs
items.body: Start with rent, software, insurance, or any recurring business cost. GigLedger converts it into a daily figure.

items.title: Add or import income
items.body: Enter a payment in seconds or import a CSV from your platform. Platform fees and net payouts stay attached.

items.title: See what's actually left
items.body: Your dashboard separates gross income, fees, costs, and true profit, then shows what to reserve for taxes.

audience.title: For work that doesn't fit one platform.
audience.body: Freelance income rarely arrives in a straight line. GigLedger is built for the mixed, monthly, messy reality of independent work.

items.label: Platform freelancers
items.body: Upwork, Fiverr, Toptal, and marketplace sellers dealing with fees, payouts, and currency changes.

items.label: Independent creators
items.body: Sponsorships, subscriptions, digital products, and direct client work in the same ledger.

items.label: Consultants and studios
items.body: Project income, recurring costs, and a clean monthly view you can share.

honesty.title: Start with what works. Add automation when it's reliable.
honesty.body: GigLedger starts with manual entries and CSV import. Platform connections come later, after the core numbers are right.
no: No tax filing on your behalf

faq.title: Questions, answered.
faq.body: The short version: we would rather be clear than overpromise.

items.a: No. GigLedger gives you an estimate and a reserve target. It does not file returns or provide tax advice.

items.q: Does it connect to Upwork or Stripe?
items.a: Not yet. You can add income manually or import a CSV. Official integrations are planned after the core ledger is stable.

items.q: What counts as a fixed cost?
items.a: Recurring business costs such as coworking, software, insurance, hosting, and accounting. Personal costs can be tracked separately.

items.q: Can I use it outside the US?
items.a: The first tax estimates are built for US self-employment. You can still use the ledger elsewhere, but tax rules vary by jurisdiction.
You can export and delete your data. We do not ask for bank passwords or Social Security numbers. See the privacy notice for details.
The first version is in development. You can try the calculator now, and sign in with Google to save your ledger.

footer.tagline: A clearer ledger for independent work.

legal.privacyDraft: Pre-launch draft. This notice must be reviewed before launch.
privacyBody: When you use “Sign in with Google”, GigLedger stores your Google account email and name, plus the ledger entries you save. Your Google password is never stored.

You can export your saved ledger from the dashboard, then request account deletion by deleting your workspace after export. Account deletion removes your Google email, name, income entries, fixed costs, and workspace settings.
Unsaved calculations remain on the current page only and are cleared when you refresh or leave the page.
This pre-launch draft still requires the legal entity, contact details, retention period, processors, and final deletion workflow before general launch.
disclaimerBody: GigLedger provides estimates for planning only. It is not a tax, legal, or accounting advisor.

You choose your own reserve rate. GigLedger may show a common range of 25%–30% for US self-employment planning. It does not calculate your actual federal, self-employment, or state tax, and it does not file a return.
Consult a qualified professional before filing a return or making a tax decision.

metrics.profitNote: Net income minus fixed costs and one-time expenses
metrics.comparisonNote: Required = days this month × daily floor

steps.title: Start with what you must pay
steps.body: Add one recurring business cost. GigLedger turns it into a daily floor before any client pays you.

steps.title: Record what you earn
steps.body: Add income and the platform fee. Net income updates immediately.

steps.title: See what is actually left
steps.body: True profit subtracts monthly fixed costs from net income. Tax reserve stays separate.

fixed.title: Fixed costs
fixed.body: Rent, software, insurance, and other recurring business costs. Each one is annualized, then divided by 365.

app.fixedVersionNote: Changes saved today use today as the effective date. Existing history is not recalculated.

income.title: Income
income.body: Record the payment amount and platform fee. The prototype uses these entries immediately.

expenses.title: One-time expenses
expenses.body: Use this for individual purchases such as outsourcing, ads, or equipment. These do not enter Daily Floor and should not duplicate a subscription already in fixed costs.
